question: Which of the following environmental factors plays an important role in deciding the sex of a developing organism in some animals?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Temperature.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In some animals, the** sex **of a developing organism is determined by the** temperature** at which the eggs are** incubated.**
 
• This phenomenon is known as** temperature-dependent sex determination (TSD).**
 
• In TSD, the sex of the offspring is determined by the temperature experienced during a** critical period of embryonic development.**
 
• This **critical period **is different for different species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In some species, such as turtles and crocodiles, warmer temperatures during incubation result in the development of more females, while cooler temperatures result in more males.
 
• In other species, such as some lizards, the opposite is true.
 
• TSD is an adaptive mechanism that allows species to adjust the sex ratio of their offspring to match the prevailing environmental conditions.
 
• However, it also makes them vulnerable to climate change, as even small changes in temperature can have significant effects on the sex ratio of their offspring.
